source: U.S. Census Bureau, pooled 1-year PUMS person files 2019 and 2021-2024
target: Share of people who report a divorce in the past 12 months, per 1,000 people aged 15+ who were married at some point in those 12 months (currently married or separated, or divorced or widowed within the 12 months). Cross-sectional one-year incidence from a single interview, not a prospective hazard or a lifetime risk.
timing_warning: Occupation and industry are the current job, or the most recent job in the last 5 years, reported at the interview, AFTER any divorce in the past 12 months. A divorce can change a job, and people in different jobs differ in age, sex, education and earlier marriages. These are descriptive rates of who reports a divorce, not effects of a job and not a forecast for a marriage.
uncertainty: 95% CI = estimate +/- 1.96 SE; SE from the 80 successive-difference replicate weights; pooled years combine replicate i across years
age_standardisation: Direct age standardisation to the pooled at-risk population (ages 15-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-64, 65+), computed in every replicate for the CI; published only when a cell has people in all five bands.
codes: OCCP: 2018 Census occupation codes (stable 2019-2024); SOC major group from SOCP; industry sector from the INDP label prefix; detailed industry from INDP. Labels from the Census PUMS data dictionaries.
